approach: A single rope over a frictionless fixed pulley carries the same tension throughout, so the pulling force equals the tension that must accelerate the block.

steps.text: The pulley is fixed and frictionless, so it only changes the rope's direction; the tension is the same on both sides of the pulley.
This same tension is the only horizontal force on the block, since the floor is frictionless.
Combine the two to solve for F.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the pulley doubles the force like a movable pulley gives F = 100 N, but this pulley only redirects the rope; it does not add mechanical advantage.
Adding an extra factor for the pulley being frictionless (as if that changed the tension relation) gives an answer other than 200 N; frictionless only means the tension is equal on both sides.
